label: UNOFFICIAL LEADS — reported by third parties, NOT verified. Nothing here has been confirmed against a league or club source, and nothing here may be promoted into data/archive.json without re-checking the original page and finding an official grounding sentence.

leads.subject: Caleb Douglas
leads.text: Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas is questionable to return with an ankle injury.
leads.verifyNext: The Dolphins' own Sept 21 transcript asks Hafley about "Caleb Douglas's ankle" and he says it is too early to tell, so the club confirms the injury but never states it happened in the game. Next check: a club sentence naming the moment.
leads.notes: Not in the verified archive. Miami is one of the clubs with no club-sourced in-game row for Week 2.

leads.text: Raiders wide receiver Dareke Young is questionable to return with a hamstring injury. He had one reception for 27 yards before going down with the injury.
leads.verifyNext: Check Raiders.com game recap/press conference for an official sentence about Young in the Week 2 game.

leads.verifyNext: Look for a Vikings.com or NFL.com sentence about Jones in the Week 2 win over Chicago.

leads.subject: Tyrique Stevenson
leads.text: Bears defensive back Tyrique Stevenson is doubtful to return with a hamstring injury.
leads.verifyNext: The archive holds Stevenson's Week 1 shoulder row; a Week 2 hamstring event would be a separate row. Needs a club or NFL.com sentence for Sept. 20.

leads.subject: Max Melton

leads.subject: Kayode Awosika
leads.reportedStatus: missed time (fibula), left the game in the fourth quarter
leads.text: Awosika left the game in the fourth quarter after suffering the injury. Trevor Penning replaced him and finished the game.
leads.verifyNext: A club sentence that places the fibula inside the Week 2 game is still missing: chargers.com confirms Harbaugh said he will "miss some time" (5 Takeaways, Sept 21) but does not say when it happened. Third-party coverage says he left in the fourth quarter.
leads.notes: The league roundup already carries Harbaugh's official line that Awosika will miss time; the official text does not say when the injury happened, so no row exists yet.

leads.subject: Dalvin Tomlinson
leads.reportedStatus: missed time (hamstring), exited in the second half and did not return
leads.text: As for Tomlinson, he exited the game in the second half and did not return.
leads.verifyNext: Find a chargers.com sentence tying the hamstring injury to the Week 2 game. Check the pregame report first: he was already listed with a hamstring issue before kickoff, which may make this an aggravation rather than a new in-game injury.
leads.notes: Pregame-versus-in-game ambiguity is exactly the case the review queue exists for.

leads.subject: Treydan Stukes
leads.text: The most notable injury to come from the Los Angeles Chargers game was safety Treydan Stukes. The rookie second-round pick had to be placed in the concussion protocol.
leads.verifyNext: raiders.com carries only a Week 2 press-conference video and the Week 2 injury report (no in-game sentence). Next check: a raiders.com article or Week 3 report that ties the protocol entry to the Chargers game.
leads.notes: Official text exists for the protocol status (NFL.com roundups, Sept 21 and Sept 23). Only the in-game origin is third-party.

leads.subject: Brett Thorson
leads.text: He came out of the game with a little hamstring. He is being evaluated now.
leads.verifyNext: Re-read the vikings.com roster-move story and the Week 3 injury report; confirm the right-hamstring listing and any practice return before treating this as current.
leads.notes: PROMOTED Sept 24: vikings.com now anchors the origin ("Thorson suffered a hamstring injury Sunday at Chicago"). Kept here as a re-check lead because the earlier reports disagreed about whether he woke up sore or left the game.

leads.subject: Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins
leads.text: Vikings defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins left the Bears game early with a hip injury; the club's Week 3 injury report lists him as limited with an oblique injury.
